summary: Founder of the S. D. Warren paper company (Westbrook, ME); John's 6th cousin 6x removed via Hammond.
bio:
Path: Lt. John Hammond → Abigail Hastings → Abigail Hastings (m. John Warren) → Samuel Warren (1704) → Joseph (1745) → John (m. Susanna Grout) → S. D. Children (all 7C5R): Samuel D. Warren II (1852–1910), co-author with Louis Brandeis of 'The Right to Privacy' (1890); Edward Perry Warren (1860–1928), art collector (the Warren Cup), who commissioned Rodin's The Kiss (Lewes version); Henry Clarke Warren (1854–1899), Pali/Buddhism scholar (Buddhism in Translations); Fiske Warren, single-tax utopian; Cornelia Warren, philanthropist.

Hammond ([R4-S1]): Samuel Warren (V, b. Watertown 18 Mar 1704, m. 1728 Tabitha Stone) -> Joseph (b. Grafton 22 Apr 1745, d. 1808, m. Lois Lyons) -> John (b. Grafton 28 Nov 1767, d. 17 Jun 1828, m. 2nd 1804 Susanna Groat) -> 'Samuel Dennis Warren, the founder of the well known firm of S. D. Warren & Co., of Boston'. With Samuel Warren (V) descending from William Hammond through Lt. John Hammond and the Hastings line, S. D. Warren is a 6th cousin 6 times removed. His sister Anna Groat Warren's son George Warren Hammond helped compile the Hammond genealogy.

media.note: Samuel Dennis Warren (September 13, 1817 – May 11, 1888) was an American paper magnate and the founder of the S. D. Warren Paper Mill in Westbrook, Maine. Noted for his benevolence and paternalism, Warren built a commercial block adjacent to the mill, which is named in his honor.
